claims.text: Varying ion density will influence the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons under low applied fields.
Varying substrate temperature will influence the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of the specified films or nanoribbons.
Varying deposition time will influence the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of the specified films or nanoribbons.
Changes in the selected deposition parameters induce changes in alloy microstructure.
Changes in the selected deposition parameters induce changes in alloy composition.
Deposition-induced microstructural changes govern the magnetocaloric response during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Deposition-induced compositional changes govern the magnetocaloric response during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Deposition-induced microstructural and compositional changes influence magnetic hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Optimized deposition parameters will enhance the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Optimized deposition parameters will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Non-optimized deposition parameters will decrease the magnetocaloric response and increase hysteresis.
Heat-transfer rate limits the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under low-applied-field conditions in genuinely low-dimensional films or patterned nanoribbons.
A lack of a significant change in both magnetocaloric response and hysteresis following systematic deposition-parameter variation would falsify the hypothesis.
